clue.text: Instrument that introduces a nursery rhyme

definitions.meaning: a kind of hand-beaten drum, originally from Asia
the words that open the old nursery rhyme about the piper's son who stole a pig

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the same doubled word: a hand drum, and the repeated name opening a children's verse.

indicators.note: the queen's letters open up the school word by sitting inside it

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword queen

explanation.surface: A queen cuts the ribbon at a new school sports field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens' reads like a royal ribbon-cutting at a school, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land or ground, especially regarding its physical features.

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means hung about listlessly, sulking
a small motorised bicycle, a means of transport

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: the past tense of mope, and a light motorbike.

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: something done badly is muddled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Oscar-winner who drives badly at the racetrack is just being natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown naturally, without artificial chemicals.

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a miler runs the mile race
taken as written

explanation.surface: A long-distance athlete plays host to an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Mailer was an American novelist, and a mailer can also simply be someone who writes letters.

indicators.note: in the old sense, without means outside, so the cancelling word surrounds the A

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or declare void
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cancels a magazine subscription that arrives regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside, putting A inside ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a yearly book or publication, such as a children's comic annual.

indicators.note: the composer is placed in the middle of the profile word

parts.note: a line or outline can be a profile
Jacques Ibert was a French composer

explanation.surface: A dissolute musician is the subject of a magazine profile.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine is a person who leads a decadent, dissolute life; used here adjectivally as decadent.

definitions.meaning: esteem or high regard for someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a detail or point and esteem or regard felt for someone.

parts.note: Com. is an abbreviation for commander
partly, in part
mental is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A commanding officer, a bit unhinged, is detained under mental health law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sectioned' suggests compulsory detention under Britain's Mental Health Act, but means divided into sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Compartmental describes something divided into compartments, that is, sectioned.

parts.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for wicket
a rap is a sharp blow

explanation.surface: In cricket, a wicket falls from a shot hit to the fielder at cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a fielding position in cricket, the bat-and-ball game, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrap is a covering, such as a shawl or wrapping.

parts.note: puréed food has been ground up
the bass is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish purée is served as a side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground bass is a repeated bass line in music, accompanying the changing upper parts.

parts.note: Anderson shelters were British home air-raid bunkers in the Second World War; the official who supervised air-raid precautions guarded them

explanation.walkthrough: The clue also hints at the answer split in two: a shelter in wartime is a war den.
explanation.definitionFit: Air-raid officials in wartime Britain oversaw shelters, and a keeper of anything, such as a prison, holds this title.

clue.text: Flighty female about to settle colour

indicators.note: the female bird's name goes round the settling word

parts.note: a pen is a female swan, a flying bird
to agree a matter is to settle it

explanation.surface: A frivolous woman finally decides on a shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' suggests capricious, but here it simply means able to fly; a swan's mate is the female in question.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea green is a bright yellowish-green shade, the colour of peas.

definitions.meaning: performing before an audience at a gig

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both performing on stage before an audience and acting jointly with others.

clue.text: In transit, cutting south of Ontario

indicators.note: in a down entry, being south of means coming below, so after

parts.note: hewing means chopping or cutting

explanation.surface: Travelling through Canada, someone is cutting timber south of Ontario.
explanation.definitionFit: On the wing means flying or travelling, so in transit.

clue.text: Excessive noise with time creates depression

parts.note: a din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: Constant loud noise over time makes someone depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dint is a dent or hollow, a depression in a surface.

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub them by ignoring them

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone snubs the Estonian head of state and is called charming for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means attractive or charming in an endearing way.

clue.text: Victorian mate holds a sovereign (or pound)

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a friend, and Victoria is an Australian state
a sovereign is a gold coin worth a pound, abbreviated L from libra

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century friend owns a gold sovereign worth one pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' suggests the 19th century but means from the state of Victoria in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber someone is to hit hard, to pound them.

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Her modest nature kept her feelings held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' reads as temperament, but signals rearranging HERMODEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother a feeling is to suppress or stifle it.

indicators.note: to be under canvas is to be inside a tent

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas
to rid is to free or clear

explanation.surface: A weapon was freed while camping under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, a weapon associated with Neptune.

indicators.note: off means not right or gone bad, so the letters go awry

explanation.surface: Something peels away to reveal a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a letter, a written note.

indicators.note: the abbreviated name is placed inside the other word

parts.note: to bag a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: George shot a duck and put it in his game bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The wigeon is a species of dabbling duck.

clue.text: Tory tours news agencies for a laugh

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the party word surrounds the other

parts.note: Con. is short for Conservative, the Tory party
the media are the news outlets

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician visits the press, purely for amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a performer one books or watches to get a laugh.

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a scamp
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A naughty child's singing ruins everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or spoil it.

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes after

parts.note: pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, a fixed mathematical relationship
a lot means many

explanation.surface: Many people rely on a relationship counsellor's guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relationship' suggests romance but means a mathematical ratio, pi.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot guides a ship into harbour, so to pilot is to guide.

clue.text: Wipe out former pupil who's properly educated

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
literate means able to read and write, educated

explanation.surface: An old boy who learned well wants to erase his school past.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to destroy completely, to wipe out.

parts.note: L, a learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate
ate away, as rust eats away metal, wearing it down

explanation.surface: An ex-student has wasted away.
explanation.definitionFit: Late can mean former or previous, as in 'the late chairman'.

parts.note: R, rex, is the abbreviation for king
someone past it is aging, getting old

explanation.surface: A deranged monarch is too old for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging means furious, wildly angry, that is, mad.

indicators.note: letters that are prepared have been made up anew, rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever image was made ready in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted representation of a person or animal.
